origin.description: Locate every word, ignoring non-word boundary segments.
origin.usage: stri_locate_all_words(str, omit_no_match = FALSE, locale = NULL, get_length = FALSE)

arguments.name: str
arguments.text: A character vector, or an object coerced to character.

arguments.name: omit_no_match
arguments.text: TRUE returns a matrix with zero rows when there is no word.

arguments.name: locale
arguments.text: NULL or "" for the default locale, or one locale identifier.

arguments.name: get_length
arguments.text: TRUE makes the second column the length. A miss on a real string is then -1.

origin.details: Equivalent to stri_locate_all_boundaries with type word and skip_word_none TRUE. Positions are 1-based inclusive code points.
origin.example:
loc <- stri_locate_all_words("ab cd")[[1]]
cat(paste0('stri_locate_all_words("ab cd") starts at ', paste(loc[, 1], collapse = ", "), '.\n'))

translation.description: Locate every word, ignoring non-word boundary segments.

arguments.name: str
arguments.text: A string, NA, or a list of those. None is an empty vector.

arguments.name: omit_no_match
arguments.text: True returns a matrix with zero rows when there is no word.

arguments.name: locale
arguments.text: None or "" for the default locale, or one locale identifier.

arguments.name: get_length
arguments.text: True makes the second column the length. A miss on a real string is then -1.

translation.details: Calls stri_locate_all_boundaries with type word and skip_word_none true. Positions are 1-based inclusive code points. Japanese word breaks are included.
translation.value: A list of matrices. Each matrix is a list of [start, end] or [start, length] rows.
translation.example:
from stringi.boundary import stri_locate_all_words
loc = stri_locate_all_words("ab cd")[0]
starts = ", ".join(str(row[0]) for row in loc)
print(f'stri_locate_all_words("ab cd") starts at {starts}.')
